1.0.0: Receive Hub: webhook trigger that fires when the selected hub sends data to the flow. HubBI resolves the webhook URL of the flow itself, so nothing has to be configured beyond the hub. Records are emitted one at a time by default, or all at once as a single list; in both modes the hub's target fields are exposed on the output port. An event carrying no records is acknowledged without triggering the flow. A flow refuses to start when a Start Hub or Start Hub With Data in it uses the same hub, which would make the flow trigger itself.
Start Hub: start a hub that does not take any data.

Start Hub With Data: start a hub with one or more records, built from the hub's source field definitions and sent in a single bulk request. .NET field types (Int32, Int64, Double, Decimal, DateTime, Date, Guid, Boolean, ...) are mapped to matching inspector input types and JSON schema types, in every notation HubBI reports them: bare (Int32), fully qualified (System.Int32) and nullable (System.Nullable`1[System.Int32]). The SourceFields and TargetFields endpoints do not agree on which one they use.

The hub picker is a dropdown of the hubs available to the connected HubBI client, so a hub is picked, never typed. Each action reads its hubs from the list that fits it: target hubs for Receive Hub, source hubs with or without post data for the two Start Hub actions.
HTTP 409 (Conflict) is treated as transient and retried, while HTTP 423 (Locked) is not retried. All other errors keep the retry engine's default classification.

Flow Test Mode: Receive Hub throws with an explanation instead of emitting an example. HubBI exposes no endpoint for reading past hub events, so any sample would have to be invented - it would match no real run and make the test pass while testing nothing. Real output requires starting the flow and sending data from the hub.

Inspector dropdown calls are cached. The hub lists back a dropdown in every component and the designer resolves them in a concurrent burst whenever an inspector opens, which the 5 req/s quota does not absorb, so the three list helpers serve source calls through lib.callEndpointCached: staticCache keyed on URL + token + client key, guarded by context.lock so a cold cache still results in a single upstream request, TTL from context.config.listCacheTTL. A flow run is never served from cache.

A hub lookup that fails behind a dropdown is logged and answered with an empty list rather than raising an error in the designer, since the inspector resolves the list before an account is necessarily connected. The same lookup in a flow run still fails loudly.

Every output port field carries an example value, so the variable picker previews what a field actually looks like instead of showing a bare key. This covers the static ports of Start Hub and Start Hub With Data, the hub and field-definition lists, the generic index / count / file options, and the per-field schemas derived from a hub definition, where the example follows the mapped .NET type.
